43-062.r: Panchsheel's five principles: respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, mutual benefit and equality, peaceful co-existence; Non-alignment is NOT one.

43-063.r: India's 'No First Use' nuclear doctrine → stated after the 1998 tests, formally adopted January 2003, under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

43-064.r: Six Points Formula for the South Asian region → presented by PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

43-065.r: USA reaffirmed Arunachal Pradesh as an integral part of India (July 2023; again March 2024, rejecting China's claim).

43-066.r: Minimum age: Lok Sabha member 25 [Art 84(b)], Rajya Sabha member 30, President 35 [Art 58(1)(b)].
43-066.h: 25-30-35: add five at each step — Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, President.

43-067.r: Minimum ages: 21 → Panchayat member; 25 → State Legislative Assembly member; 30 → State Legislative Council member; 35 → President of India.

43-068.r: Oaths: President → faith and allegiance to the Constitution; SC Judges → upholding Constitution and law; MPs → faithful discharge of duties; Union Ministers → secrecy of information.

43-069.r: Extra-constitutional power → one not found in the Constitution's provisions; e.g., Planning Commission, made by a Cabinet resolution, yet it wielded power over Centre and States.

43-070.r: Chronology: Air India nationalised (1953) → Imperial Bank renamed State Bank of India (July 1955) → first elected communist government, EMS Namboodiripad (April 1957) → Goa joins India.

43-071.r: District Collector as District Magistrate → law and order, control over police, passport/visa and foreigners' matters; land revenue is his role as Collector.
43-071.t: Land revenue comes under the 'Collector' hat, not the 'District Magistrate' hat.

43-072.r: Rajni Kothari (book 'Politics in India') → called the District Collector an 'Institutional Charisma'.

43-073.r: Wrong: Madam Cama was not the first woman INC President — Annie Besant was (32nd session, 1917, Kolkata); Cama hoisted India's flag at Stuttgart, 22 August 1907.

43-074.r: True: right to life and personal liberty can't be suspended in Emergency; Vice-President removed by Rajya Sabha resolution approved by Lok Sabha. NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission, January 1, 2015.

43-075.r: Two wrong: 8th Schedule has 22 languages (not 18) since the 92nd Amendment, 2003; Queen Victoria's Proclamation (November 1, 1858), not Charter Act 1813, is the 'Magna Carta'.
43-075.c: No answer printed: both (b) and (d) are incorrect, so the question has two answers.

43-076.r: All true: HC judges serve till 62 [Art 217(1)]; national party needs recognition in 4+ States; Lok Sabha Speaker decides Money Bills [Art 110(3)]; cognizable offence → arrest without warrant.

43-077.r: Suicide → a crime whose doer cannot be punished; only the attempt was punishable (IPC Section 309); Law Commission's 210th report urged deleting Section 309.

43-078.r: Param Vir Chakra → highest military decoration; instituted 26 January 1950; four 'Indra Vajra' replicas on the medal; can be won more than once; 21 awardees till 31 December 2025.

43-079.r: All three false: Bharat Ratna/Padma Awards aren't titles under Art 18(1); Padma Awards (1954) interrupted twice (1978-1979 and from 1993); Bharat Ratna not capped at five a year.

43-080.r: Bharat Ratna 2024 (announced February 9, 2024, posthumous) → P.V. Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh and M.S. Swaminathan.

43-081.r: First Bharat Ratna (1954) → C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman; of the options, S. Radhakrishnan.

43-082.r: Bharat Ratna instituted 1954; first awardees C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman. Non-Indians: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987, first), Nelson Mandela (1990).

43-083.r: Highest civilian award of India → Bharat Ratna; Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan were both instituted in 1954.

43-084.r: Gandhi Peace Prize (instituted 1995, Gandhi's 125th birth anniversary) jury → PM (chair), Chief Justice of India, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha — not the President.

43-085.r: Gandhi Peace Prize 2021 → Gita Press, Gorakhpur; prize instituted 1995 on Gandhi's 125th birth anniversary; open to all regardless of nationality.

43-086.r: Outstanding Parliamentarian Award (from 1995): Murli Manohar Joshi 2009, Arun Jaitley 2010, Karan Singh 2011, Sharad Yadav 2012.
43-086.h: Initials J, J, K, S run in alphabet order with the years 2009 to 2012.

43-087.r: Bihar → record nine coalition governments between 1967 and 1971.

43-088.r: Joyita Mondal (West Bengal) → India's first transgender Judge, of a Lok Adalat at Islampur (North Dinajpur), at age 29.

43-089.r: Press Council of India → statutory quasi-judicial body, set up 1966 under the Press Council Act, 1965.

43-090.r: Justice Markandey Katju → Press Council chairman from October 5, 2011. Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai's first term ended December 2025; she was reappointed for three years the following April.
43-090.c: Option (b) Markandey Katju chaired the Council from 5 October 2011; the book marks none as the chair changes. Its 'no permanent chairperson' line is outdated: Justice Desai was reappointed for a second term.

43-091.r: Regionalism in India arises from uneven development, fear of losing cultural identity and desire for political prominence — all of these.

43-092.r: National Water Development Agency → set up July 1982 as an autonomous society (Societies Registration Act, 1860); National Water Board formed September 1990.

43-093.r: Chronology: Tashkent Agreement (10 January 1966) → Indo-Soviet Treaty (August 9, 1971) → Shimla Agreement (2 July 1972) → Farakka Accord (1977; final 1996).

43-094.r: Bangladesh created December 1971: India intervened on 3 December 1971; Pakistani Army surrendered on 16 December 1971.

43-095.r: Lashkar-e-Taiba → founded 1990 in Kunar Province (Afghanistan) by Hafiz Muhammad Saeed, Zafar Iqbal and Mahmoud Mohammad Bahaziq.

43-096.r: LTTE banned by India, Sri Lanka, USA and many others; its chief Prabhakaran was killed in the Sri Lankan Army's 2009 operation.

43-097.r: Djibouti Code of Conduct (adopted 29 January 2009) → against piracy and armed robbery on ships in the Western Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden.

43-098.r: Operation Checkmate → Sri Lanka; Operation Cactus → Maldives; Operation Blue Star → Punjab; Operation Siddharth → Bihar.

43-099.r: 'Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya' → motto of All India Radio.

43-100.r: Wrong pair: Silent Valley movement → Dr. Salim Ali, not Baba Aamte (Narmada Bachao, wildlife); Apico → P. Hegde; Chipco → S.L. Bahuguna; Narmada Bachao → Medha Patkar.

43-101.r: Chief of Defence Staff → military advisor to the Defence Minister on tri-service matters; first CDS General Bipin Rawat (1 January 2020); now General Anil Chauhan.

43-102.r: Not true: CDS chairs Defence Acquisition Council — the Defence Minister does. CDS: age limit 65, permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee, member of Defence Planning Committee (NSA chairs).

43-103.r: CDS (Head, Department of Military Affairs) → permanent Chairman of Chiefs of Staff Committee and principal military advisor to Defence Minister; does NOT command the three Service Chiefs.

43-104.r: Wrong pair: Armoured Corps Centre and School is at Ahmednagar (Maharashtra), not Jabalpur; Southern Air Command Thiruvananthapuram, Eastern Naval Command Visakhapatnam, Army Medical Centre Lucknow.

43-105.r: Army operational commands: 5 in June 1999, 6 now — Western (Chandi Mandir), Eastern (Kolkata), Northern (Udhampur), Southern (Pune), Central (Lucknow), South Western (Jaipur, from 2005).
43-105.c: Printed (c) 6 clashes with the explanation: in June 1999 there were 5 operational commands, option (a); 6 counts the Training Command too. South Western Command (2005) later made it 6 operational.

43-106.r: Equal ranks: Army Major = Air Force Squadron Leader = Navy Lieutenant Commander (only pair 3 is right; pairs 1, 2, 4 are wrong).
43-106.t: Brigadier's Navy equal is Commodore, not Commander; Lieutenant Colonel's is Commander.

43-107.r: Army Lieutenant Colonel = Navy Commander = Air Force Wing Commander; Colonel = Captain = Group Captain; Brigadier = Commodore = Air Commodore.
43-107.h: Navy names sit one step 'up': Army Colonel → Navy Captain, Lt Colonel → Commander.

43-108.r: Operation Sadbhavana → Army's work for upliftment of local people in remote areas (basic needs); idea: human security is key to national security.

43-109.r: Border Security Force → raised 1 December 1965; guards the international border with Pakistan; HQ Delhi.

43-110.r: Border guards: BSF → Pakistan and Bangladesh; ITBP → China; SSB → Nepal and Bhutan; Assam Rifles → China and Myanmar.

43-111.r: Home Guards → voluntary auxiliary to police, raised by State governments under State Acts (not the Central Government); aid internal security and emergencies; Border Wing battalions exist.

43-112.r: Internal Security Academy → Mount Abu (Aravali Range, Rajasthan), under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

43-113.r: BHARATPOL → online portal for international police cooperation, developed by the CBI; launched 7 January 2025 by Home Minister Amit Shah.

43-114.r: First Law University in India → National Law School of India, Bangalore, established August 1987.

43-115.r: First law university → National Law School of India, Bengaluru; when this was asked, Kerala and New Delhi had none (NUALS Kochi, NLU Delhi came later).

43-116.r: Castes are being politicised (emerging as pressure groups) and casteism is rising in politics — both true, but R does not explain A.

43-117.r: Uttarakhand (2003) → gave OBC status to Gurkhas and two other communities (Ghrit Chahang, Uthalia Vora).

43-118.r: Scientific socialism → Karl Marx (gave socialism a scientific base; regarded as father of communism).

43-119.r: Morstein Marx's four types of bureaucracy → Guardian, Caste, Patronage, Merit.

43-120.r: 'Gandhian Constitution for Free India' (1946) → drafted by Gandhian economist Shriman Narayan Agarwal on Gandhi's ideas, not by Gandhi.

43-121.r: Atul Kohli → The Success of India's Democracy; Granville Austin → Working a Democratic (Constitution); Penderal Moon → Divide and Quit; Alan Gledhill → The Republic of India.

43-122.r: 'Democracy and Development in India: From Socialism to Pro-Business' (2009) → Atul Kohli.

43-124.r: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (NRI Day) → 9 January, marking Gandhi's return from South Africa (1915); first PBD convention 9 January 2003; new format since 2015.
43-124.h: 9 January 1915: Gandhi, the greatest pravasi, came home.

43-125.r: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas convention began 2003 (yearly till 2015, then biennial); announced by PM Vajpayee on 8 January 2002 after the Lakshmimal Singhvi Committee report.

43-126.r: 'The India Way' (2020) and 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024) → S. Jaishankar, Minister of External Affairs.

43-127.r: National Voters' Day → 25 January (correct); Constitution Day → 26 November (not 27 January); Human Rights Day → 10 December (not 29 January).

43-128.r: Good Governance Day → 25 December (Atal Bihari Vajpayee's birthday), announced in 2014.

43-129.r: Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan → launched by the Central Government under 'Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav' for the 75th Independence anniversary (AKAM began 12 March 2021).

43-130.r: Correct pairs: Argentina → worst economic crisis (President Javier Milei from 10 December 2023); Sudan → army vs paramilitary war. Turkey has not left NATO.

43-131.r: Chechnya → Russia (North Caucasus); Darfur → Western Sudan (not Mali); Swat Valley → Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan (not Iraq).

43-132.r: Berber-speaking people (Amazigh, original inhabitants) → North Africa, e.g. Algeria and Morocco; their language differs from Arabic.

43-133.r: Arctic Council (Ottawa Declaration, 1996) → eight members: Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Russia, USA; Japan and UK are not members.
43-133.h: Arctic eight = five Nordic States + Canada, Russia, USA.

43-134.r: India-Sri Lanka Accord, 1987 → kept Sri Lanka's integrity and merged northern and eastern provinces; did NOT give complete freedom to a Tamil State.

43-135.r: First woman Prime Minister of any country → Sirimavo Bandaranaike, Sri Lanka, 1960; PM three times (1960-65, 1970-77, 1994-2000).

43-136.r: Sweden → first EU country to recognise the State of Palestine (October 2014); Palestinian flag first raised outside UN HQ on 30 September 2015.

43-137.r: UN observed 1975 as the International Year for Women.

43-138.r: International Day of Persons with Disabilities → 3 December, observed annually since 1992.

43-139.r: International Day of Non-violence → 2 October (Gandhi's birthday); fixed by UNGA resolution of 15 June 2007.

43-140.r: ULFA (United Liberation Front of Assam) → separatist outfit in Assam, founded 7 April 1979, seeks a sovereign Assam; banned in 1990.

43-141.r: People's War Group → founded by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah on 22 April 1980 in Andhra Pradesh.
